svg.title: Intlify overview: compiler-based localization architecture
svg.desc: Source-first UI, explicit Message Intent declarations, and standalone MF2 messages enter host-specific producers. Prebuilt Library Manifests enter the language-neutral compiler model directly. The checked graph and complete requirement plan feed both explicit localization synchronization and deterministic application build workflows. Synchronization separates candidate validation, governance decisions, and atomic Store publication. The Store snapshot feeds build verification. Final linking branches into a Host Lowering Backend and Target Exporter. Their matching target outputs converge at Release Assembly, the final static compiler stage, which emits one immutable Release Snapshot. Downstream, an authorized publication transaction creates a Release Publication Record, the host verifies that record and activates a Release reference, and execution admission checks the deployment-selected Release. One Release Snapshot may have multiple publication records for different destinations. Conforming production execution then uses the admitted Release and matching outputs through either a runtime-backed or capability-checked ahead-of-time path.
svg.text: Source-first authoring → governed localization → Release Snapshot → publication and activation → bounded execution
Application-owned messages are authored in source; simple UI can remain ordinary host-language text.
